skills.name: Understanding ε and δ
skills.description: Define ε (epsilon) as a small positive number representing a desired level of accuracy. Define δ as a small positive number ensuring the function f(x) is within ε of the limit L when x is near c.

skills.name: Formal Limit Definition
skills.description: For a limit to exist, for every ε > 0, there must exist a δ > 0 such that if 0 < |x - c| < δ, then |f(x) - L| < ε.

skills.name: Reading Graphs
skills.description: Analyze graphs of functions to determine the value of a limit as x approaches a specific value.

skills.name: Applying the Constant Rule
skills.description: The limit of a constant is the constant itself.  If f(x) = c, then lim (x→c) f(x) = c.

skills.name: Applying the Power Rule
skills.description: The limit of x^n as x→c is c^n, provided the function is continuous at x=c.  For example, lim (x→2) x^2 = 2^2 = 4.

skills.name: Calculating Limits of Products
skills.description: If lim (x→c) f(x) and lim (x→c) g(x) exist, then lim (x→c) [f(x)g(x)] = [lim (x→c) f(x)] * [lim (x→c) g(x)].

skills.name: Calculating Limits of Quotients
skills.description: If lim (x→c) f(x) and lim (x→c) g(x) exist and g(c) ≠ 0, then lim (x→c) [f(x)/g(x)] = [lim (x→c) f(x)] / [lim (x→c) g(x)].

rules.name: Sum and Difference Rules for Limits

skills.name: Applying Sum and Difference Rules
skills.description: The limit of a sum or difference of functions is the sum or difference of their limits.  lim (x→c) [f(x) ± g(x)] = [lim (x→c) f(x)] ± [lim (x→c) g(x)].

skills.name: Understanding One-Sided Limits
skills.description: Left-hand limit: lim (x→c⁻) f(x) (approaching c from the left). Right-hand limit: lim (x→c⁺) f(x) (approaching c from the right).

skills.name: Checking for Existence of Limit
skills.description: A limit exists if and only if the left-hand limit and the right-hand limit exist and are equal.

skills.name: Understanding the ε-δ definition of a limit.
skills.description: This is the fundamental definition of a limit.  It states that for every ε > 0, there exists a δ > 0 such that if 0 < |x - c| < δ, then |f(x) - L| < ε.  Focus on interpreting the meaning of each component of the definition.

skills.name: Differentiating x^n (where n is a real number)
skills.description: If f(x) = x^n, then f'(x) = n * x^(n-1).  This is a fundamental rule and will be used extensively.  Practice applying this rule with various exponents.

skills.name: Differentiating a constant
skills.description: If f(x) = c (where c is a constant), then f'(x) = 0.  This represents the rate of change of a constant function is zero.

skills.name: Differentiating a constant multiplied by a function
skills.description: If f(x) = c * g(x), then f'(x) = c * g'(x).  This rule simplifies differentiation of functions that are constant multiples of other functions.

skills.name: Differentiating the sum or difference of two functions
skills.description: If f(x) = u(x) ± v(x), then f'(x) = u'(x) ± v'(x).  Apply this rule when differentiating expressions with additions or subtractions.

skills.name: Differentiating the product of two functions
skills.description: If f(x) = u(x) * v(x), then f'(x) = u'(x) * v(x) + u(x) * v'(x).  This is crucial for differentiating products of functions.

skills.name: Differentiating the quotient of two functions
skills.description: If f(x) = u(x) / v(x), then f'(x) = [u'(x) * v(x) - u(x) * v'(x)] / [v(x)]².  Practice applying this rule carefully.
